summary: Tested driver document photos and the official logo on the backend and frontend. Backend: 41/42 pytest pass (19 new doc tests and 23 regression tests). The regression fixtures were updated for the new vehicle_name and 4-photo requirement. Frontend (375x667 web preview), all passing: /driver shows the 4-tile grid; the camera/gallery sheet opens; 4 gallery uploads via file chooser each show their image in the tile; the photos-required hint disappears; submit -> Under review with tiles read-only. Admin Drivers tab shows 4 thumbnails per pending driver; tapping opens a full-screen preview; Approve removes the card and the user becomes approved. Logos: full logo on the language screen; travoo-logo on auth and home (header and footer); travoo-logo-mark on booking confirmation; icon/splash assets are the official logo. Regression smoke passes: login -> home search Bengaluru->Chennai -> 3 results -> trip detail -> instant booking -> confirmation. Bugs found: (1) admin can approve a user who uploaded only 1 photo and never submitted; (2) SVG and non-image bytes accepted (stored XSS risk); plus minor UX issues. No deprecated Expo packages detected.

critical.issue: The guard only checks that a driver_documents record exists. But upload_document upserts that record on the first photo upload. Result: a user who uploaded 1 photo and never called /driver/verification can be APPROVED (reproduced: returns 200). The check should require submitted_at, or driver_status == 'under_review'. Reference: server.py:1151 and server.py:498

Image validation trusts the client Content-Type only. image/svg+xml with a <script> is accepted and served back from the API origin as image/svg+xml (verified 200). Plain text sent as image/jpeg is also accepted. On web, tokens sit in localStorage on the same origin, and the file URL carries ?token=. If an admin opens the link directly, this is a stored-XSS / token-theft vector. Fix: allow only jpeg/png/webp/heic, check magic bytes (or Pillow verify), and send Content-Disposition/X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Reference: server.py:486-492, 513

minor.issue: The JWT in the query string can leak into proxy/access logs, and expo-image caches it as part of the URL key. Consider short-lived signed file tokens.
The whole body is read before the 8MB size check, and re-uploads leave orphaned files in db.files and storage.
Any status can be re-reviewed, e.g. approving an already-rejected or not_submitted user. There is no status-transition check.

ui_bugs.issue: Submitting without a vehicle name shows the raw Pydantic text 'vehicle_name: String should have at least 2 characters'. There is no client-side validation or friendly message.

issues: Thumbnail labels are 9px dark text placed directly over the photo with no scrim. They are unreadable on dark photos (admin.tsx:139). Use at least 11-12px on a scrim, like DocPhotos does.
Thumbnails are about 71x71: fine as touch targets.
The sheet uses animationType='slide'. Buttons are briefly off-screen while it animates (only matters for automated tests).

action_items: HIGH: admin_review_driver must require a submitted verification (driver_documents.submitted_at present, or user.driver_status == 'under_review'), not just an existing driver_documents record (server.py:1151).
HIGH: upload_document: whitelist image/jpeg, png, webp and heic (reject svg), validate magic bytes, and add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on /api/files responses.
LOW: Add client-side validation and friendly messages for the verification form (vehicle_name, etc.) instead of raw Pydantic errors.
LOW: Make the admin document thumbnail labels readable (bigger font plus scrim).
critical_code_review_comments: upload.ts correctly branches expo/fetch vs browser fetch: good for native multipart.
DocPhotos permission pre-prompt flow is good. On web, permissions auto-grant and the gallery opens a file chooser (verified working).
Logo `light`/`tagline` props are accepted but ignored (Logo.tsx:18). Harmless, because headers wrap the logo in a white pill.
Removed old/orphan file docs are never cleaned (db.files grows on every re-upload).

On web, the doc sheet needs ~1s after tapping a tile before the gallery button is clickable. Use page.expect_file_chooser + set_files.
rca_of_issue: Partial-upload approval: upload_document does an upsert into driver_documents ({photos.kind, user_id}). admin_review_driver's 'has submitted' guard is `find_one({'user_id': uid})`, which is therefore true after any single upload. Repro: register -> upload profile photo -> admin POST review approved -> 200, and the user becomes an approved driver without legal name, licence or RC.
